title: Need workflow advice
author: Embarrassed_Staff412
selftext:
Hi, I'm new on using AI for game dev, currently working on a 2d mobile game in unity

Workflow: right now I only use ChatGPT for image and code generation, the plus point I really like is that the chat feels like chatting with human. 

Question: 
I have heard of other AI tools like bezi and claude for unity, are those tool chatlike too? 

I only have tried ChatGPT for AI game dev, if anyone have tried another tool like bezi and claude or anything else, please tell me the comparison of those tools vs ChatGPT in term of game dev

Also if it's not too much, please share your current workflow with AI. 

Thanks!

comments.author: Microtom_
comments.body: Gemini 3 pro on AI studio has 10 free prompts per day. It's better than the free Chatgpt. The Gemini website, which differs from AI studio, has 2 free nano banana pro prompts, which is better than the Chatgpt image model.

replies.body: This is for image generation right? Alright man, would try it later, thanks for the input

replies.body: Gemini is top tier at rapid prototyping but it simply doesn’t match Codex 5.3 or Claude for developing a complete game. Eg. building a house, Gemini can put up a beautiful house but once you step inside everything is disjointed.

comments.author: KimmTsh
comments.body:
To answer your questions first:

* **Claude:** Yes, it works exactly like ChatGPT (chat interface). A lot of Unity devs actually prefer it for C# scripting right now because it tends to handle larger context better and hallucinates code less often.
* **Bezi:** This is quite different—it's a 3D collaborative design tool (think Figma but for 3D/Spatial), so it's not a text chatbot like the others.

**My Current Workflow for 2D:** I’ve actually shifted a bit from ChatGPT for art. Currently, I use **Gemini 3 Pro** to generate my initial base sprite sheets.

However, the issue with raw AI gen is getting the *rest* of the assets to match that first sheet. To fix that, I use [AssetMeld](https://assetmeld.com/?utm_source=reddit). I basically feed the Gemini sprite sheet into it to "lock in" the art style, and then generate all my specific variants from there while still keeping the same style. It solves the consistency problem, so you don't end up with assets that look like they came from 5 different games.

comments.author: Abdullah_3254
comments.body:
I’ve tried a few tools ChatGPT and Claude feel more chat based and good for ideas and code Bezi feels more connected to Unity and helps inside the project itself

I usually use ChatGPT for planning and scripts then Unity tools for testing and fixing things mixing them works best

And mixing it sounds great. What are your thoughts on bezi after using it for a while? Any pro n cons?

comments.author: Classic-Ninja-1
comments.body: Both claude and bezi has there own benefits like bezi is good for unity as it runs in unity editor and claude has the logic mastery which is needed for the game dev. i have been using Claude and traycer for game development too and it works out well as it combines the planning and execution very well.

comments.author: EmmaABCabc9
comments.body: Bezi is chat like but works inside Unity so it can read your project and help with scripts, assets, and debugging. Claude is more like ChatGPT but better for coding and logic. Most people use ChatGPT for ideas and code, then Bezi or Unity tools for in engine stuff.
